column1: # The pack's own version — the one thing about core-es a human versions rather
# than the build derives.
# Columns: version
# Content packs version independently of the app: a dataset ships without an app
# release, and does. `package.json` is the app's version and has nothing to say
# about this one.
# `items` is the sentence-and-word-card total the version was cut at, and it is
# here to stop this file going stale. The version used to be a literal inside
# `scripts/build-dataset.ts`, written once when the pack held 443 sentences and
# never touched again — four dataset expansions later it still said 0.1.0, and
# Settings displayed that to every learner. Now the build reports a disagreement
# and `tests/data/pack-version.test.ts` fails on one, so adding or removing
# content forces an edit here, with the version on the same line.
# Which number to move: a new topic, a new set of sentences or a new word is
# additive, so it is the minor. The major is for a change that could invalidate
# what a learner has practised — retiring items in bulk, renaming topic slugs,
# changing the level scheme. A wording or accent fix changes no count, needs no
# bump, and should not get one.
# `updated` is the date this version was cut, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. **Authored, not
# stamped**, and that is not laziness: the build has to be reproducible — CI fails
# when a rebuild changes `public/packs` — so a date read from the clock would make
# every build differ from the last and the drift check useless. It sits on this row
# because it changes with the version, and because the item-count guard already
# forces an edit here whenever content moves, which is exactly the moment the date
# should change too. The build rejects a date it cannot parse, or one in the
# future.
# Run `npm run build:data` to learn the current count; it prints it either way.
